decision: MobileNetV3-Large (V2 Experiment 004), exported to ONNX and executed through cv2.dnn
framing: Selected for the competition runtime. This is not a claim that it is the best model in general; SigLIP2 zero-shot is measurably better out of domain and was not selected.
rationale: Serving needs no deep-learning framework. The ONNX graph runs through cv2.dnn, so the deployment image carries opencv-python and numpy instead of torch, torchvision or transformers. That is the single largest container-size lever available, and it removes an entire dependency class from the attack and maintenance surface.
Smallest deployable artifact with acceptable behaviour: 11.35 MB, against 1431 MB for the SigLIP2 encoder that the best out-of-domain candidate requires.

Best worst-external accuracy among the self-contained CNNs (70.4%, against 69.3% for ResNet50 and 68.8% for EfficientNet-B0), which is the criterion that matters for a deployed inspector meeting unfamiliar captures.
Parity with the framework-native reference is measured, not assumed: 200/200 predicted classes agree with torch plus torchvision preprocessing.
Running inference through OpenCV deepens substantive OpenCV 5 usage in a competition judged on exactly that, rather than confining OpenCV to pre- and post-processing.

rejected.name: SigLIP2 strict zero-shot
rejected.reason: The accuracy-optimal choice, deliberately not taken. Requires a 1431 MB encoder plus transformers and torch at serving time — roughly 126x the selected artifact — and cannot be executed through cv2.dnn. The out-of-domain advantage is real and is recorded as a limitation of the selection, not dismissed.

rejected.name: SigLIP2 + linear probe
rejected.reason: Probe is ~20 KB but inherits the same 1431 MB encoder and dependency burden for lower external retention than SigLIP2 zero-shot.

rejected.name: EfficientNet-B0
rejected.reason: 1.5 points better in domain but 1.6 points worse on the worst external domain, and a larger artifact. In-domain accuracy is not the deciding criterion.

rejected.name: ResNet50
rejected.reason: Roughly eight times the weights of the selected model for lower worst-external accuracy.

rejected.name: DINOv2 + linear probe
rejected.reason: 330 MB encoder plus transformers, for worse external behaviour than the selected 11 MB model.

rejected.name: CLIP + linear probe
rejected.reason: 571 MB encoder and the weakest external retention of the foundation probes.

rejected.name: Custom CNN (V2 baseline)
rejected.reason: Collapses out of domain. Small, but smallness does not compensate for 34.6% worst-external accuracy.

rejected.name: V1 Keras CNN (2018)
rejected.reason: Requires TensorFlow 1.12 on CPython 3.6.7, which cannot coexist with the Python 3.11 competition runtime. Retained as a historical reported figure only.

accepted_tradeoff: A deployable 11 MB model that holds 70.4% on its worst external domain was preferred over a 1431 MB one that holds 86.3%. The gap is material and is stated openly: the selected model is more likely to be wrong on unfamiliar produce photography, which is precisely why the capture gate and the escalation path exist.
revisit_if: Container size or cold start turns out not to be the binding constraint on the chosen AWS runtime.
A distilled or quantised foundation encoder becomes exportable to ONNX at a size comparable to the selected model.
Measured external performance on self-captured competition imagery diverges materially from the Experiment 014 figures.
claim_boundary: The selected model predicts visible surface condition across three fruit types. It makes no food-safety, edibility, contamination or internal-spoilage claim.
